speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked	the Minister for Education (Schools) (a) whether there are sufficient places for autistic students awaiting entry into special needs institutions; (b) what is the current average waiting time; and (c) what are the plans to make available more educational opportunities and support for students with autism.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: Many of these children with ASD attend different SPED schools, including those that serve students with other disabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: But some parents have a preference to place their child with ASD into a SPED school of their choice and, in particular, an ASD-specific school.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: Where there is a waitlist, MOE has, upon request, facilitated placement into an alternative SPED school which is appropriate for the child's specific disability profile.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: Children diagnosed with ASD have diverse needs and may require more specialised and intensive intervention to support their learning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: MOE, together with NCSS, will continue to closely monitor SPED school places, infrastructure, quality, as well as staffing levels to ensure the timely placement of students with moderate to severe ASD needs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: First, I would like to ask the Minister of State if there is a specific planning ratio of students with ASD to the number of places in the schools.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Second, how are the manpower planning programmes put in place, because we do understand that it is difficult to recruit, train and hire the correct and qualified people to staff these places?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: With respect to both issues, the needs of the children are very diverse and the label "ASD" is insufficient to adequately describe the complexity of the needs these children may have, from the mild to the moderate to the severe, as well as the co-existence of other challenges, other diseases and other disabilities that the child may have at the same time.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, there is no fixed planning ratio that you can apply across the whole spectrum of diseases, needs, children and disability profile.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The different schools have developed different expertise in particular needs, particular profiles, particular disabilities and particular diseases.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: They have their own norms to cater to the functional outcomes of executing their curricular plans and serving the needs of their children.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: This also applies to the manpower planning issue.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: As we can imagine, the two are very closely related.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There is a difficulty in hiring and identifying staff that have the appropriate aptitude and skills, as well as the enthusiasm for this type of work.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But we are confident that we will be able to do so, going into the future.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Just a quick question for the Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Earlier, in his initial reply, he mentioned that the Ministry has seen an increase in the number of students across the autism spectrum.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Does the Minister of State have a sense of those numbers?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If the Member would like to file a question for that, I would certainly have them ready for him.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The increase in ASD is a phenomenon that is being noticed around the world in all types of communities.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Quite a number of residents that I meet during our house visits do feedback that there is a shortage of such places, particularly in the western part of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I urge the Minister of State that in coming up with new centres, to consider building them in the west.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The issue for the SPED schools and the children that they serve is that the expertise is quite profile-specific.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: For some of the children with certain types of profiles of disease and disability, their numbers are not large and so, the centres which have the expertise are effectively serving the entire nation.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Going forward, in planning, we will look at the skills-mix as well as the staffing mix of all the SPED schools to see what we can do to optimise the delivery of these services for these children.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Would the Ministry consider working closely with Pathlight School to set up more schools, where the Ministry would put in a lot more support in terms of funding and manpower resource?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Certainly, while the total capacity within the SPED schools is more than sufficient to cater to the children, we do have to pay some attention to the skills and facilities to ensure that each child will have a place appropriate to their profile of needs and challenges.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: That is part of the panel that is looking at the implementation of compulsory education for special needs children, going forward.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The Minister of State mentioned about the increased capacity in due course.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Does the Minister of State have a timeline and what sort of waiting time could parents expect?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Also, does the Ministry have a sense of how many are on the waitlist and who do not have a place in school?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I know some on the waitlist actually have places somewhere else.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: There are also those on the waitlist who are not in school.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: A large part of the issue for the waiting lists currently is the choice the parents have and assert, with respect to which of the SPED schools they would like to place their children in.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In relation to the skills shortages that we have discussed, is the Government looking into the possibility of establishing in Singapore a basic degree course in special needs education?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, there is a good mix of backgrounds and skills within the educators and professionals that serve in the special education space.
